section: Rashtrakutas - Dantidurga, Govinda III, Amoghavarsha (Kavirajamarga), Krishna I
subsections: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)
Court poets - Kannada Ratnatraya and patrons

accepted.s: Who among the following overthrew Kirtivarman II, the last ruler of the Badami Chalukyas?
accepted.x: Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II and laid the foundation of Rashtrakuta power around 753 CE.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–event association and distinguish the founder from later military rulers.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Dhruva:
1. He was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to proceed towards northern India.
2. He defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala.
3. He subdued the Eastern Chalukyas and the Gangas of Talakad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dhruva was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to move north, defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala, and subdued the Eastern Chalukyas and the Gangas of Talakad.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the ruler’s complete military profile before selecting the inclusive combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a military achievement of Govinda III?
o: Sacking Kannauj in the reign of Indra III
Defeating Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reaching the Himalayas
accepted.x: Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and is said in the Sanjan plates to have reached the Himalayas.
accepted.tq: Separate the military achievements of successive Rashtrakuta rulers instead of matching all northern campaigns together.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Amoghavarsha I — Construction of Manyakheta
2. Indra III — Sacking of Kannauj
3. Krishna III — Victory over the Cholas at Takkolam
4. Krishna I — Patronage of Ponna
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Ponna was patronised by Krishna III, not Krishna I, making statement 4 false.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped patron–ruler pair after confirming the three established ruler–event links.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Rashtrakuta rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Govinda III
B. Dantidurga
C. Amoghavarsha I
D. Dhruva
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The sequence is Dantidurga, Dhruva, Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I. Their approximate reign periods were 753–756, 780–793, 793–814 and 814–878 respectively.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest rulers first, then place the two intervening reigns by their dates.

accepted.s: Amoghavarsha I is particularly associated with which of the following combinations?
accepted.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, was associated with Kavirajamarga, and is described as a Jain ruler or patron.
accepted.tq: Use a cluster of contributions to identify the ruler rather than relying on a single isolated fact.

accepted.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler is stated to have been born in a military camp?
accepted.x: Amoghavarsha I, who ruled from 814 to 878, is noted as having been born in a military camp.
accepted.tq: Test the unusual biographical detail directly, with neighbouring rulers as distractors.

accepted.s: The defeat of the Cholas at Takkolam is associated with which Rashtrakuta ruler?
accepted.x: Krishna III defeated the Cholas at Takkolam and patronised the Kannada poet Ponna.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–battle association and avoid confusing Krishna I’s Ellora monument with Krishna III’s military victory.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the end of the Rashtrakuta line is correct?
o: Paramara Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta; Tailapa II later overthrew the line.
Khottiga defeated Paramara Siyaka II on the Narmada and captured Manyakheta.
Tailapa II was defeated by Khottiga and restored Rashtrakuta rule at Manyakheta.
Krishna III ended the Rashtrakuta line after losing Manyakheta to the Cholas.
accepted.x: Paramara Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta. Tailapa II of the Kalyani Chalukyas subsequently overthrew the Rashtrakuta line around 973 CE.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal of victor and defeated ruler in the final phase of a dynasty.

accepted.s: Kavirajamarga, generally dated to about 850 CE, is best described as:
o: The earliest work on Kannada poetics, associated with Amoghavarsha I
The first Sanskrit champu composed by Trivikrama Bhatta
A Sanskrit Jain text written by Ponna
A Kannada biography of Rishabhadeva written by Jinasena
accepted.x: Kavirajamarga is associated with Amoghavarsha I and is regarded as the earliest work on Kannada poetics.
accepted.tq: Combine the work, language, date and subject instead of matching the title only by sound.

accepted.s: Prashnottara Ratnamalika is correctly described as:
o: A Sanskrit Jain text associated with Amoghavarsha I
A Kannada work of Pampa on the life of Rishabhadeva
A Sanskrit mathematical treatise by Mahaviracharya
accepted.x: Prashnottara Ratnamalika was associated with Amoghavarsha I and is identified as a Sanskrit Jain text.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two works associated with Amoghavarsha I by their language and literary character.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Nalachampu was written by Trivikrama Bhatta. Halayudha was the author of Kavirahasya.
accepted.tq: Identify the incorrect author–work pairing after separating the closely associated Sanskrit works.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pampa’s Adipurana is a Kannada work concerning the life of Rishabhadeva.
2. Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana.
3. Pampa was a Telugu-origin poet associated with Kannada literature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Pampa wrote a Kannada Adipurana, Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana, and Pampa is described as Telugu-origin or Telugu-born.
accepted.tq: Retain the distinction between two Adipuranas and the poet’s regional origin.

accepted.s: Who wrote Ganitasarasangraha, a Sanskrit work on mathematics?
accepted.x: Ganitasarasangraha was written by Mahaviracharya and is identified as a Sanskrit mathematical work.
accepted.tq: Use the subject–author link to distinguish the mathematician from the court poets.

accepted.s: The first champu among the following is:
accepted.x: Nalachampu, written by Trivikrama Bhatta in Sanskrit, is identified as the first champu.
accepted.tq: Recognise the descriptive clue ‘first champu’ and match it with the exact title.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kavirahasya was written by Halayudha in Sanskrit. Santipurana was written by Ponna in Kannada, Nalachampu by Trivikrama Bhatta in Sanskrit, and Vikramarjuna Vijaya by Pampa in Kannada.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and eliminate the swapped poet and language combinations.

accepted.s: Which ritual did Dantidurga perform at Ujjain to legitimise his authority?
accepted.x: Dantidurga performed the Hiranyagarbha ritual at Ujjain.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler–ritual–place triad directly, using other royal rituals as plausible distractors.

accepted.s: Dantidurga was contemporary with which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
accepted.x: Dantidurga, whose reign is placed around 753–756 CE, was contemporary with Eastern Chalukya Vijayaditya I.
accepted.tq: Compare approximate reign periods to identify the contemporary ruler.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Rashtrakuta capitals is correct?
1. The early seat was in the Elapura or Ellora region.
2. Dantidurga’s inscription is found in the Dashavatara cave at Ellora.
3. Manyakheta was built by Amoghavarsha I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The early Rashtrakuta seat was in the Elapura region, Dantidurga’s inscription is in Ellora’s Dashavatara cave, and Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the early Elapura seat and inscription from the later capital of Manyakheta.

accepted.s: Manyakheta, also known as Malkhed, is located in present-day:
accepted.x: Manyakheta or Malkhed is in Karnataka and was built by Amoghavarsha I.
accepted.tq: Use the present geographical location to resolve the historical capital question.

accepted.s: Which of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Balhara, or Vallabharaja, was a title generally used for Rashtrakuta kings, not exclusively for Govinda III. Nripatunga and Viranarayana were titles of Amoghavarsha I, while Prabhutavarsha was associated with Govinda III.
accepted.tq: Reject an over-specific title assignment when the title was used generally for a dynasty’s kings.

accepted.s: The title ‘Viranarayana’ is associated with:
accepted.x: Viranarayana was one of the titles of Amoghavarsha I.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive royal title with its ruler rather than with a similarly named successor.

accepted.s: Arab writers used the term ‘Balhara’ for:
o: The Chola kings who ruled at Takkolam
accepted.x: Balhara is the Arab form associated with Vallabharaja and was used generally for Rashtrakuta kings. Al-Masudi was a contemporary source for this usage.
accepted.tq: Avoid the trap of assigning a dynastic title to one particular ruler when it had broader usage.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict is correct?
o: The conflict continued for approximately two centuries.
It was exclusively a conflict between the Rashtrakutas and the Cholas.
It began only after the fall of the Rashtrakutas in 973 CE.
It was confined to a single battle during Dantidurga’s reign.
accepted.x: The Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict continued for approximately 200 years and involved repeated struggles with the Eastern Chalukyas.
accepted.tq: Use the approximate duration to distinguish a prolonged dynastic conflict from a single campaign.
accepted.sec: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)

accepted.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have fought 108 battles against Rashtrakuta forces?
accepted.x: Vijayaditya II is stated to have fought 108 battles against Rashtrakuta forces.
accepted.tq: Treat the distinctive numerical figure as a direct ruler–event identifier.
accepted.sec: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dhruva acted through Vemulavada Arikesari I against the Eastern Chalukyas.
2. Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi in marriage to Dhruva.
3. Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and assumed the title Viranarayana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. These facts describe important Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya relations during the reigns of Dhruva and Amoghavarsha I.
accepted.tq: Check the sequence of alliance, marriage and battlefield outcome across the Vengi conflict.
accepted.sec: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)

accepted.s: What was the immediate result of the battle of Takkolam in 949 CE?
o: Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II and captured Takkolam.
Krishna III defeated Chola king Parantaka I, and Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.
Dhruva defeated Pallava ruler Nandivarman, and Rajaditya became king.
Amoghavarsha defeated Parantaka I and annexed Vengi.
accepted.x: At Takkolam in 949 CE, Krishna III defeated the Cholas under Parantaka I, and the Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, victor, defeated ruler and notable casualty to identify the correct battle account.
accepted.sec: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)

accepted.s: After the death of Amoghavarsha I, which ruler of Vengi defeated Krishna II?
accepted.x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II after the death of Amoghavarsha I.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Eastern Chalukya rulers by the specific Rashtrakuta ruler they defeated.
accepted.sec: Conflicts with Vengi, Pallavas and Cholas (Takkolam)

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Poet)
a. Pampa
b. Ponna
c. Ranna
d. Swayambhu

List-II (Association)
i. Apabhramsha poet linked to the court
ii. Patronised by Krishna III
iii. Patronised by Arikesari II
iv. Patronised by Tailapa II

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II, Ponna by Krishna III, Ranna by Tailapa II, and Swayambhu was an Apabhramsha poet linked to the court.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure patron–poet pair and use elimination for the remaining court associations.
accepted.sec: Court poets - Kannada Ratnatraya and patrons

accepted.s: The Kannada ‘Ratnatraya’ traditionally refers to which group?
accepted.x: The Kannada Ratnatraya consisted of Pampa, Ponna and Ranna, the three celebrated Kannada poets associated with major royal patrons.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete literary triad rather than one poet or one patron.
accepted.sec: Court poets - Kannada Ratnatraya and patrons

accepted.s: Who was the patron of Pampa and the ruler of Vemulavada associated with the Rashtrakuta feudatories?
accepted.x: Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II of the Vemulavada Chalukyas, who were Rashtrakuta feudatories. Arjuna in Pampa’s epic was modelled on this patron.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a poet’s immediate feudatory patron from the imperial Rashtrakuta ruler.
accepted.sec: Court poets - Kannada Ratnatraya and patrons

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Pampa’s literary association is correct?
1. He wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya, also known as Pampa Bharata.
2. Arjuna in the epic was modelled on his patron Arikesari II.
3. He was hailed as a Telugu-born poet despite writing in Kannada.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Pampa wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya in Kannada, modelled Arjuna on Arikesari II, and is noted as a Telugu-born or Telugu-origin poet.
accepted.tq: Combine title, patronal influence and regional identity while avoiding the language–origin confusion.

accepted.s: Which of the following was an educational centre associated with the Rashtrakuta period?
accepted.x: Salotgi in the Bijapur region is mentioned as an educational centre associated with the Rashtrakuta period.
accepted.tq: Test the institution–location pairing using nearby political centres as distractors.
accepted.sec: Court poets - Kannada Ratnatraya and patrons

accepted.s: Which of the following best reflects the cultural significance of the Rashtrakuta period?
o: It marked the disappearance of Kannada literature and the exclusive growth of Sanskrit.
It saw the replacement of rock-cut architecture by wooden temple construction.
It was significant only for naval expansion in the eastern coast.
It marked a golden age of Kannada and the zenith of rock-cut art, including Ellora Kailasa and Elephanta.
accepted.x: The Rashtrakuta period is described as a golden age of Kannada and as the zenith of rock-cut art, represented by the Kailasa temple at Ellora and Elephanta.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines the period’s literary and architectural contributions without an extreme reversal.

accepted.s: Which ruler was visited by Sulaiman, who regarded him as one of the four great kings of the world?
accepted.x: Sulaiman visited the court of Amoghavarsha I and considered him one of the four great kings of the world.
accepted.tq: Use the foreign visitor–ruler association to identify the correct reign.

accepted.s: Vijayaditya II of the Eastern Chalukyas is associated with which cultural and religious contribution?
o: Construction of 108 Shiva temples and the naming of Vijayawada
Construction of the Kailasa temple at Ellora
Establishment of Manyakheta as the Rashtrakuta capital
accepted.x: Vijayaditya II is associated with the construction of 108 Shiva temples and with the naming of Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Match the regional contribution to the correct Eastern Chalukya ruler rather than to a Rashtrakuta monarch.
